book_title: Kunooz al-Hikmah: The Stored Treasures of Wisdom for the Masters of Infallibility

preface.title: How to Read a Book of Stored Secrets

chapters.title: The Author and His Only Book
chapters.rationale: The opening frame identifies the book's title, its meaning of partial infallibility, and the single treatise left by Sayyidna Ali ibn Hibatullah.

chapters.title: Praise, the Three Human Natures, and the Unknowable God
chapters.rationale: The doxology's own argument: the special, middle, and lowest nasut, and the equality of first and last creature in failing to know God.

chapters.title: The Prophet, His Brother, and the Veiled Successors
chapters.rationale: The salutation moves through Muhammad's ascent, Ali as his very self, Fatimah as greatest hujjah, and Hasan and Husayn as trustee and manifester of occultation.

chapters.title: Blessings on the Chain: Imams, Gates, and the Du'at of Najran
chapters.rationale: The remainder of the salutation names the Imams, the hidden Imam, and the individual du'at down to the migration to Najran and Habuna.

chapters.title: Before the Words Begin: Refuge, the Call to Prayer, and the Prayer for the Da'i
chapters.rationale: The second lecture's opening treats ta'awwudh, the adhan, the order of praise and salawat, and the supplication for the da'i's protection.

chapters.title: The Reluctant Answerer: How These Questions Came to Be Written
chapters.rationale: The introduction proper: questions arrive from the children of the da'wah, the author pleads incapacity, names the book, and binds readers by covenant.

chapters.title: What Was There Before Origination
chapters.rationale: The first question and its answer: nothing preceded the World of Origination, and the questioner's account of the veils is corrected.

chapters.title: The Fifteen Ranks of the Repentant and How Far We Fell
chapters.rationale: The same answer's second half turns to the penitent souls, their fifteen categories, and the illusion of equality that caused the fall.

chapters.title: The Sphere That Rises From Where It Stands
chapters.rationale: The second question concerns the encompassing sphere, the sun's light, and the ascent of the Imam's soul through the Sacred House.

chapters.title: Subtle Essences: What Rises From the Dead and What Feeds the Living
chapters.rationale: This stretch traces the riyat from the grave through moon and spheres into the Imam's body, ablution, and the fast.

chapters.title: Three Veils, Four Ranks, Twenty-Eight
chapters.rationale: The answer closes by matching the Imam's three veils and four ranks to the clauses and letters of the testimony of faith.

chapters.title: The Middle Way and the Heart Beneath the House
chapters.rationale: Lecture five opens on neither miserliness nor extravagance, then turns to the true heart beneath the Frequented House.

chapters.title: Registers of Rank: Who Stands Where, and the Twenty-Ninth
chapters.rationale: A sustained meditation on rank-lists, designations passed over, the special status of the twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth, and the disjoined letters.

chapters.title: The Black Stone and the Cycles of Return
chapters.rationale: The third question: the Rukn as remnant of Amir al-Mu'minin, testing in the da'wah, and whether glorification may be applied to him.

chapters.title: Beneath the Ka'bah: Lowlands, Waters, and the Well of the Jinn
chapters.rationale: The fourth question on the four lowlands, their channels, the well where Ali fought the jinn, and the stations of pilgrimage.

chapters.title: Harun to Musa: The Successor Who Dies Before the Prophet
chapters.rationale: The fifth question turns on Ali's station as Harun, the exchange of veils between the mim and the 'ayn, and Ja'far al-Sadiq's veiling through Isma'il.

chapters.title: The Fifth Intellect and the Verdict on the Caliphs
chapters.rationale: The answer identifies Husayn as the fifth intellect and the Fatimi powers, framed by an extended historical indictment of the first caliphs.

chapters.title: Returning as You Left: The Doctrine of the Second Cycle
chapters.rationale: The sixth question asks whether one returns at the same rank, and the answer fixes rank, place, era, and the settling of accounts.

chapters.title: Offerings, Trials, and the Making of a Da'i
chapters.rationale: The same answer's tail gathers examples of designation, offering, and hardship among the du'at, closing with Hajj and pure intention.

chapters.title: The Cold Edges of the World: Where the Opponents Are Cast
chapters.rationale: The seventh question locates the opponents of Imams and prophets at the frozen extremities and describes their punishment and the winds.

chapters.title: Rubies, Elephants, and Believers: The Summit of Each Kind
chapters.rationale: The eighth question on jewels and rubies, their gathering, dissolution, and succession to the celestial spheres.

chapters.title: Visiting the Graves: Traces, Intercession, and Free Will
chapters.rationale: The ninth question on the visitation of graves, the illumination cast toward the remains, and the choice that makes man alone answerable.

chapters.title: The Knife and the Name: Sacrifice at Mina
chapters.rationale: The tenth question on the slaughter of the sacrifice at Mina, the expulsion of the sensory soul, and what becomes lawful.

chapters.title: Standing at 'Arafat
chapters.rationale: The answer on Mount 'Arafat, the revelation descending there, and the covenant sealed at Ghadir Khumm.

chapters.title: Prayer Outside the Island: The Eleventh Question
chapters.rationale: The eleventh question on Sulayman ibn Hasan, his son at the two wells, and the unique permission to lead prayer beyond the three islands.

chapters.title: Seven Ranks Within Every Rank
chapters.rationale: The answer distinguishes trustee from established du'at and the sevenfold grading within each rank, sealed by the covenant of secrecy.

chapters.title: The Mahdi, the Qa'im, and the Straight Path
chapters.rationale: The first appended question distinguishes the Mahdi of concealment from the Qa'im and reads the straight path as the line of succession.

chapters.title: Rolling Up the Sky: Cycles Without End
chapters.rationale: The last question on the folding of the heavens, the endless alternation of concealment and unveiling, and the scribe's closing colophon.
